answer: Sybil resistance here rides a stake-backed admission bond that pays only while an identity stays unlinked. Each new address must lock more capital than one address can earn, so splitting into fake identities multiplies locked stake, not payout. A trust anchor co-signs each onboarded address; if its cluster outgrows quota the cluster is slashed. One caught Sybil sends a ripple across everyone sharing that anchor, and rewards decay toward their nadir as anchors pile up. Far from a cheap haven, N identities cost N bonds plus a forfeit per collapse, so the play only raises the attacker's bill.
